single.reason: The G>A change is C>T on the opposite strand and may create an ETS-family motif in the TERT promoter, where mutant-motif recruitment of GABPA is a well-established route to increased TERT expression in cancer.
ETS1 can recognize the same ETS-like sequence created by the alternate allele, potentially increasing TERT promoter activity.
ELF1 recognizes ETS-family motifs, so the alternate allele may increase its occupancy at this cancer-associated TERT regulatory region.
